clue.text: Dialect actors needed for radio programme

parts.note: a broad accent or broad speech is a strong regional dialect
the cast of a play is its company of actors

explanation.surface: Performers must put on regional accents for a wireless play.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast is to transmit over the air, so a radio show is a broadcast.

clue.text: Put up a centre of Latvian nationalism

parts.note: to rig up a tent or mast is to put it up, erect it

explanation.surface: A slogan about raising a symbol of Baltic patriotism.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Latvia is the natural focus of its national feeling.

clue.text: Regular income from a Parisian night in New York

indicators.note: the French word for night sits within the abbreviation for the American city

parts.note: nuit is the French word for night, as a Parisian would say

explanation.surface: Someone earns a steady living from a French evening spent in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word; 'in' places NUIT between N and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuity pays a fixed sum each year, a regular income bought with a lump sum.

clue.text: One who reaps the harvest from a heavy fall

definitions.meaning: someone who gathers in a crop is a reaper of it
to come a ... is to take a heavy fall

explanation.definitionFit: A grower or reaper of crops is one sense; the idiom 'come a cropper' gives a nasty tumble.

clue.text: Revolutionary cooking device tips up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word tips is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A rotating oven gadget keeps tipping over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' is the definition: a roasting spit revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting spit is a rod turned over a fire so meat cooks evenly as it rotates.

clue.text: They cleaned up a stack on the lotteries

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: a chimney stack, the tall flue above a roof
sweeps is short for sweepstakes, a kind of lottery

explanation.surface: Some winners made a killing on the lottery draws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaned up' suggests winning big money, but it is the definition: these workers literally clean soot out.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who brush soot from flues have literally cleaned up after the fire.

clue.text: Maybe they lead through the heart of the countryside

definitions.text: Maybe they lead through the heart of the countryside

parts.words: Maybe they lead through the heart of the countryside
parts.note: main routes are named after the blood vessels that carry blood from the heart, and these run across the country

explanation.definitionFit: Main highways are named after the vessels leading from the heart, and they carry traffic across country.

clue.text: G&S herein told recollection embodying appeal

definitions.text: G&S herein told recollection embodying appeal

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take a further letter into their body
read as re-collection, the letters are gathered again in a new order

parts.note: the initials of Gilbert and Sullivan, the Victorian comic opera pair
O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O Lord'

explanation.surface: A memory of a Gilbert and Sullivan story, told here with a plea in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle G, S and HEREINTOLD and put O inside. Gilbert and Sullivan were the Victorian writing team of comic operas, and this is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: This Venetian-set comic opera is a Gilbert and Sullivan work, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Welcome sign of the palsy?

parts.note: a greeting gesture read whimsically as a symptom: palsy makes the limbs tremble

explanation.definitionFit: Clasping palms is a gesture of greeting, and palsy makes the limbs tremble.

clue.text: If not, it is a confession that one has no monopoly of sagacity

definitions.meaning: meaning or else, in different circumstances

definitions.text: a confession that one has no monopoly of sagacity
definitions.meaning: split in two, the word says that people besides oneself are clever too

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means 'or else'; split, it admits that others are clever too.

clue.text: Purposes of first-class writing

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a British label for the best quality; crosswords often treat the 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: goals or intentions are the targets one has in view.

clue.text: Devout politicians living off immoral earnings

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the people who do this

parts.note: pi is informal British slang for pious, devout
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Pious MPs are secretly running a vice racket.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is British slang; MPs are British members of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Men who take the money earned by prostitutes are described as living on immoral earnings.

clue.text: In it one may keep dry sweet wine

definitions.text: In it one may keep dry
definitions.meaning: a canvas shelter keeps a camper out of the rain
an old name for a deep red sweet Spanish wine

explanation.definitionFit: A camper's canvas shelter keeps off rain; also a dark sweet wine from Spain.

clue.text: Bowl when the university team is batting

parts.note: BAs, Bachelors of Arts, are graduates who make up a university side
in cricket the side that is batting is said to be in

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction to bowl while the college side is at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl' looks like the cricket verb but is the noun, a basin. 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide round open vessel for washing is a bowl.

clue.text: Young scout joined by an army mercenary in Angola

parts.note: a Cub is a junior member of the Scout movement

explanation.surface: A junior scout signs up with a soldier of fortune in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 1970s and 1980s Cuban troops fought in the Angolan civil war, so the definition was topical.
explanation.definitionFit: Havana sent soldiers to fight in Angola's civil war, so such a fighter was from Cuba.

clue.text: I eat dry mash of nutritious nature

indicators.note: to mash something is to squash it into a new form, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone eats dry mashed potato for its food value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mash' reads as potato but rearranges I EAT DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to diet and nourishment, as in a dietary supplement.

clue.text: Usual procedure in breaking an itinerary

indicators.note: one word breaks into the middle of the other, splitting it apart

parts.note: a route is the planned way of a journey, an itinerary

explanation.surface: Interrupting a travel plan disrupts the usual schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a regular fixed way of doing things.

clue.text: Unfriendly house provided with access to field

parts.note: a stile is a step letting walkers over a fence into a field

explanation.surface: A grumpy householder grudgingly lets walkers through to the meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: A stile, common in British countryside, is a set of steps over a fence or wall. 'provided with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Antagonistic or unfriendly behaviour is hostile.

clue.text: Former wife got a job as a model-undraped?

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

parts.words: got a job as a model
parts.note: a model who sat for an artist posed

explanation.surface: A former wife became an artist's nude model.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncovered and naked, with nothing draped over the body, is exposed.

clue.text: One doesn't make a summer drink

definitions.meaning: the proverb says one such bird does not make a summer
to drink is to gulp down

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'one swallow doesn't make a summer'; and to gulp down a drink.

clue.text: South American custom is to provide German food

parts.note: usage is established custom or practice

explanation.surface: It is a Latin American custom to serve German dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Wurst is a German speciality, minced meat in a skin.

clue.text: Was familiar with new-speak

indicators.note: speak means the clue word is said out loud, where it matches the past tense of know

parts.note: the word new as heard

explanation.surface: A nod to Orwell's invented language, Newspeak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new-speak' recalls Orwell's Newspeak, but 'speak' tells you to sound out NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of know: to be acquainted with something.

clue.text: Talk the leg off an iron pot or a bit off the kettle

definitions.text: Talk the leg off an iron pot
definitions.meaning: an idiom for talking endlessly, holding forth
the projecting part of a kettle that pours

explanation.definitionFit: To hold forth at length; also the pouring lip that sticks out of a kettle.

clue.text: Part of the theatre brought down by Gotterdammerung

definitions.meaning: the highest gallery seats in a theatre
Wagner's opera title means the Twilight of the Deities, whose downfall it shows

explanation.definitionFit: The cheap top balcony is nicknamed 'the gods'; Wagner's opera shows the deities' downfall.

clue.text: Ain't otherwise antagonistic

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in another way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Isn't it rather hostile, said differently?
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something is being opposed, antagonistic.

clue.text: Novel companion for Nelson

definitions.meaning: Lady Hamilton, by first name, was the lover of Admiral Lord Nelson

explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen wrote a book of that title; Lady Hamilton, Nelson's mistress, bore the name.

clue.text: A main drama production leading to a channel contest

definitions.text: A main drama production leading to a channel contest

parts.words: A main drama production leading to a channel contest
parts.note: a great sea drama set out across the ocean and ended in a battle in the English Channel in 1588

explanation.walkthrough: The 1588 fleet from Spain sailed to fight England in the Channel. 'production' hints that A DRAMA rearranges into the second word, but nothing in the clue supplies the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip II's invasion fleet sailed against England and was fought in the Channel in 1588.

clue.text: Presumably a central figure in merchandising

definitions.text: Presumably a central figure in merchandising

parts.words: Presumably a central figure in merchandising
parts.note: the trader who stands between maker and buyer is jokingly pictured as standing at the centre

explanation.definitionFit: A dealer between producer and consumer stands in the middle of a sale.
